preconditions.description: The input consists of integers n (number of vertices) and m (number of edges) satisfying the given bounds.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v for u, v in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge (u, v) in the input is a unique pair of distinct vertices within the valid range.
The input contains no duplicate edges (each pair (u, v) appears at most once).

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'Yes' if exists_string(s, n, edges) else stdout.strip() == 'No'
postconditions.description: The first line of output is 'Yes' if and only if there exists a string s of length n over {'a', 'b', 'c'} such that the graph G constructed from s matches the given edges. Otherwise, it is 'No'.
If the answer is 'Yes', the second line contains exactly one string s of length n over {'a', 'b', 'c'} that satisfies the graph condition. Otherwise, no such line exists.

postconditions.expression: all(c in {'a', 'b', 'c'} for c in s) if 's' in locals() else True
postconditions.description: The string s (if provided) consists only of the characters 'a', 'b', and 'c'.

postconditions.expression: len(s) == n if 's' in locals() else True
postconditions.description: The string s (if provided) has exactly n characters.

postconditions.expression: all((u != v and ((s[u-1] == s[v-1]) or (abs(ord(s[u-1]) - ord(s[v-1])) == 1))) == ((u, v) in edges or (v, u) in edges) for u in range(1, n+1) for v in range(1, n+1)) if 's' in locals() else True
postconditions.description: The string s (if provided) produces a graph where edges exist between vertices u and v if and only if their corresponding characters in s are equal or adjacent in the alphabet ('a'-'b' or 'b'-'c').
